summary: Carson T. Schütze is a linguist who studied at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology from 1992 to 1997. He took up a post at the University of California, Los Angeles in 1997 and taught Edward Garrett.

Catherine Bell was a scholar in religious studies and sinology. She studied under Joseph M. Kitagawa at the University of Chicago from around 1976 to 1983, and served as Bernard J. Hanley Professor of Religious Studies at Santa Clara University (1985–2008).

Catherine Cornille works in religious and Buddhist studies. She studied at KU Leuven (~1979–1989) and the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (~1982–1984), and served as Associate Professor of Comparative Theology at Boston College around 2005.

Catherine Ella Blanshard Asher was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. She earned her PhD at the University of Minnesota (~1975–1984), where she later served as Assistant Professor from around 1984 to 2023.

Catherine Ludvik is a scholar of religious, Buddhist, and Japanese studies. She earned her PhD from the University of Toronto under David Waterhouse, also studying with Antonino Forte and Werner Knobl. She has held posts at Stanford, Doshisha, and Kyoto Sangyo universities.

Catherine Prueitt is a scholar of philosophy, Indology, and religious studies. She studied at the University of Rochester and Emory University under John D. Dunne and Laurie L. Patton, and was attested as an Assistant Professor at the University of British Columbia in 2026.
Cathy Cantwell works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD at the University of Kent by 1989 and held a post at the University of Oxford in 2002.

Cecil Bendall was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Cambridge under Edward Byles Cowell and Theodor Benfey. He held positions at the British Museum, University College London, and the University of Cambridge, where he became Professor in 1903.

Cecil Y. Lang studied at Duke University (~1937–1941) and held academic posts at Yale University (~1949–1950) and the University of Chicago (~1967–1970). He served as Professor of English at the University of Virginia from around 1970 to 1991.

Ch'ing-mao Cheng was a scholar of Sinology and Japanology. After degrees from National Taiwan University and Princeton, he held posts at UC Berkeley and the University of Massachusetts Amherst, later founding National Dong Hwa University, where he served as Founding Chair.

Chack-fan Lee, active in Buddhist studies, completed his education at the University of Hong Kong (~1965–1970) and the University of Western Ontario (~1970–1972). He later served as Pro-Vice-Chancellor at the University of Hong Kong from 1994 to 2015.
Chaesong Kim is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. Kim pursued doctoral studies at the University of Tokyo, attested in 1995, where they studied under Yasunori Ejima.

Chagdud Tulku Rinpoche was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology figure. He studied under teachers including Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje, Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, Tromge Trungpa Rinpoche, Khenpo Dorje, and Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, and taught Albion Moonlight Butters and Alwyn Fischel.

Chaim Rabin was a linguist who studied at SOAS University of London and the University of Oxford. He held academic posts at the University of Oxford from 1941 to 1956 and at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem from 1956 to 1986.

Chaisit Suwanvarangkul is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He held researcher positions at Kyoto University and the University of Delhi, and was attested in 2015 as a Lecturer in Buddhist Studies at the University of Otago.

Chakravarthi Ram-Prasad, a philosopher and scholar of Indology and religious studies, earned a doctorate at Oxford. He held research fellowships at Trinity College, Oxford, and Clare Hall, Cambridge, before holding professorships at Lancaster University, attested from 2000 through 2026.

Chamnong Adivadhanasit, active in religious and Buddhist studies, earned a BA from Chulalongkorn University. In 2012, he was attested as a Professor in the Faculty of Social Science at Kasetsart University and a part-time instructor at Chulalongkorn University.
Champa Thupten Zongtse is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He held posts at the University of Göttingen, attested in 1991 and in 2009 as a Lecturer.
Chandra R. de Silva was a historian. He was attested as a Professor at the University of Ceylon in 1991 and later as Dean of the College of Arts and Letters at Old Dominion University in 2006.

Chandrabhal Tripathi was an Indologist who earned his doctorate at the University of Göttingen under Ernst Waldschmidt (~1956–1961). He held positions at Göttingen, the University of Cologne, and served as Professor at the Free University of Berlin (~1974–1994).
